Divergence: rdflib/plugins/sparql/algebra.py:755-757 returns Update(prologue, []) for an empty or declarations-only request, where reference algebra.py:751-752 returns a bare list. The reference list breaks its own API: prepareUpdate("") would raise AttributeError when setting `_original_args` (processor.py:34), and evalUpdate([]) would raise at update.py:279. The base returned [] and evalUpdate was a no-op, so the reference regresses g.update("") and processUpdate(g, ""). The candidate keeps base behavior and makes the return type uniform, so this is an accepted valid alternative and not a failure.

initNs and base are applied at prepare time: processor.py:33 calls translateUpdate(parseUpdate(...), base, initNs); algebra.py:755-757 applies translatePrologue(q.prologue[0], base, initNs) on the empty path, and the loop applies it for non-empty requests.
initBindings are applied at evaluation time: update.py:256 (evalUpdate) builds the QueryContext, and sparql.py:229-233 copies initBindings into ctx.bindings, which the solution reflects.
Reuse is safe: evalInsertData/evalDeleteData (update.py:77-104) only read u.triples/u.quads, so repeated evaluation of one prepared object does not mutate the algebra.

Empty input (algebra.py:755-757) becomes a no-op Update, preserving the base behavior of g.update("") and processUpdate(g, ""). Declarations-only input keeps its prefixes in the returned prologue, which matches the Update container's purpose. The reference fails both cases, so the candidate extends it correctly.
